name: Olive-Grey
lede: Olive-grey is a green shade of grey, also called Scotch grey, and named for the olive.

sections.title: What the name covers
sections.body: Paterson defines *olive grey* as a green shade of grey and says it is also called *Scotch grey* [1]. His entry for *greystone* is the same: an olive grey [1]. The word *olive* itself points to the tree's leaves and fruit [2]. The same dictionary also glosses *nutria* as an olive grey [1]. Several names share one plain description [1].

sections.title: Between grey and green
sections.body: Paterson defines it as a shade of grey, with green as the modifier [1]. It sits near [[olive]], [[olive-green]] and [[sage]] on the green side, and near [[grey]] and [[taupe]] on the neutral side [1][3]. Paterson also defines *grège* as an olive grey [1].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch here is #939485, a mid-light neutral with a slight green-yellow cast [3]. Screen colors for historical names are approximate, and the books give no pigment recipe for this name [1][3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This is one of the most common colors in the ColorHub archive: 2,130 of 23,781 paintings, about 9%, hold it across at least 5% of the canvas, as photographed [3]. The strongest Western matches are Salomon van Ruysdael and Meindert Hobbema, each with 10 canvases, and the Chinese painter Shen Zhou has 8 [3]. Two-thirds of matches are highlight colors, a third mid-tones [3].
